html:
SMTO-CTX-0019 — SMTO can't find a file you attached

GUID: 46ca5613-fd4b-43b9-b230-d871e3d0961f
Slug: context-reference-invalid
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • An attached file in this request is not available to this conversation. It may have been removed, or it was attached in a different conversation. Nothing was read from it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Remove the attached file from the message you are about to send by selecting the × on its label near the message box. The old attachment points to a file this conversation can no longer use.
  2. Select the Add context button next to the message box, choose Add files to conversation, and pick the same file from your computer. Attaching it here gives this conversation its own copy it is allowed to read.
  3. If the file was first attached in another conversation, attach the same file again here from your computer instead of reusing the old attachment. Files attached in one conversation are not automatically shared with others.

What success looks like

  • The file shows as attached under the message box and the task reads it without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't attach a different file in its place unless that is really the file you want SMTO to use.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • ContextStore rejected a context reference: the ID is malformed, its source or file body is missing, the conversation has been deleted, or the source belongs to another conversation and has no grant here.

What this means

  • Context references require valid shape, an existing retained source and a grant in the requesting conversation; a matching name alone supplies none of these. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • Context references require valid shape, an existing retained source and a grant in the requesting conversation; a matching name alone supplies none of these.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare context identity, retained bytes and conversation grants; distinguish a deleted source from an existing source owned by another conversation.

How to fix it

  • Check the context_id in Technical details: it must match ctx_ followed by 32 hex characters, have a native_context_sources row, an on-disk body under the context store, and a native_context_grants row for this conversation (or be retained_reusable). Re-attach the intended file in this conversation, or link it explicitly from its owning conversation; do not substitute a different context ID.
  • Select existing context from the owning conversation or its retained artifacts. Reattach only the intended supported context; do not invent resource identities.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended reference resolves to existing bytes with a valid grant in the requesting conversation.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
